item.title: Hollow tree offers bats winter shelter
item.description: A hollow or rotting tree in the garden may look like dead wood, but it actually provides a valuable refuge for wildlife. In autumn, bats, which feed primarily on insects, actively search for food to build up fat reserves for hibernation. item.title: 86-year-old Carole Wade once sang backup for Elvis impersonators
item.description: Carole Wade (86) went viral last year when she sang Fleetwood Mac's „Landslide" during a karaoke afternoon at a senior center in Dallas, moving the audience. item.title: Audrey Hepburn refused to have her wrinkles removed
item.description: Audrey Hepburn was known for her classic beauty and accepted aging with grace. She always rejected plastic surgery and was proud of her wrinkles. During her work as a UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador, photographer John Isaacs selected a photo showing her smile with wrinkles. item.title: Common garden birds recognize faces and sometimes bring gifts
item.description: Many people unknowingly have a small nature reserve in their backyard, with birds such as robins, house sparrows, cardinals, jays and tits. Although these birds are less famous than crows or ravens, they turn out to be surprisingly good at building bonds with humans. item.title: British shopkeeper Ada Le Poidevin's wartime resistance act on Guernsey revealed 40 years later
item.description: The courage of British shopkeeper Ada Le Poidevin, who hid three British soldiers on Nazi-occupied Guernsey during the Second World War, has come to light forty years after her death. Her 79-year-old niece Liz Walton uncovered the story thanks to photographs, diaries and data from Ancestry.com. In 1940, Le Poidevin and her husband Walter Bourgaize sheltered three stranded British servicemen...

item.description: A cell therapy originally developed against cancer is proving helpful for stiff person syndrome, a rare autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks the central nervous system. item.description: A young great horned owl was struck by the truck of driver Ashley Moffitt while she was traveling 65 miles per hour in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania. The bird became wedged in the truck's air deflector and remained there until Moffitt stopped 70 miles down the road. item.description: A stray cat that had been fed by hospital staff in Izmir, Turkey for some time suddenly carried one of her kittens inside one morning. She walked fearlessly through the corridors, seeking help. Staff members examined the kitten and its siblings together with a veterinarian. item.description: A woman shared a story on Quora about her therapist that went viral after counselor Danielle Wunker posted it on Facebook. When she was going through a difficult period and couldn't even do the dishes, her therapist advised her to simply run the dishwasher two or three times instead of scrubbing the dishes first. item.title: Chester Zoo saves endangered Malaysian peacock pheasant chicks with foster mother and rubber glove
item.description: Chester Zoo was the only zoo in Europe this year to successfully hatch a Malaysian peacock pheasant. Only 15 of these endangered birds are being raised in captivity across European zoos. When a young mother abandoned her first egg, keepers placed it with a bronze-coloured peacock pheasant, who took on the role of foster mother. A second egg was hatched...

item.title: Florist in Cuincy places unsold flowers on forgotten graves
item.description: A flower shop in Cuincy doesn't throw away its unsold flowers from All Saints' Day. Instead, the owner takes them to the cemetery, where she places them on graves that appear to have been forgotten. The gesture of solidarity has moved many people online.

item.title: Aromatic herb border brightens vegetable garden without spending money
item.description: With three simple and free tricks, you can keep an aromatic herb border in your vegetable garden structurally sound, harmonious and highly productive. A quick check after rainfall or storms, manual weeding along the edges and regular compost application are sufficient to achieve results. This approach requires no extra investment yet ensures a well-organized and fertile vegetable garden.

item.description: Don't put away your garden tools just yet: November is a strategic month for the vegetable garden. It's the ideal time to sow and plant six extremely hardy vegetables. item.title: Eleven trees and shrubs should not be pruned this autumn
item.description: To get through the winter well, eleven common tree and shrub species are better left unpruned entirely in autumn. Cutting wood or branches during this period causes the plant to lose its flower buds directly or makes its overall structure more vulnerable. By refraining from pruning in the fall, these species remain stronger and better protected against the cold months...

item.title: Heat pump leasing saves French families €9,800
item.description: From November 17, 2026, lower-income French households can lease a heat pump with an average subsidy of €9,800, financed through the CEE scheme. The decree, published on November 10 in the Journal officiel, bundles installation, maintenance and electricity consumption into a single monthly payment, comparable to the old heating bill. item.title: Solar parks in Gobi Desert reduce sandstorms
item.description: A new Chinese study shows that solar parks in the Gobi Desert slow down dust storms and improve air quality in cities downwind. The 42 solar parks, together covering more than 13,000 square kilometers, reduce monthly dust emissions by 352,400 tons. item.description: Synthetic fertilizer is produced in factories operating at 450°C and releases around 450 million tons of CO2 annually. item.description: Scientists are testing a cyborg reef: part artificial, part natural, to help coral reefs suffering from heat and disease. item.description: Researchers at Worcester Polytechnic Institute calculate that bamboo can deliver fuel at commercial scale for just $2.75 per gasoline-gallon-equivalent. item.description: A 2019 study in the Journal of Social and Personal Relationships shows that friendship takes time: 50 hours for a casual friend, 90 hours for a true friend, and 200 hours for a close friend.
